transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start off, can you tell me what brings you in today?

I’m here because for almost two years I haven’t been able to shake this feeling—really, it feels more like certainty—that after a commission I worked on, a few people in the ensemble started quietly working against me.

It’s things like schedule changes, where people get seated, small comments during rehearsals… on their own they can sound like nothing, but together it feels very deliberate. They’ll show me emails or notes that are supposed to explain it, but it doesn’t really convince me. I still feel like they’re undermining my work.
Besides these beliefs about being undermined, have you ever heard voices or seen things that other people don't seem to notice?
No, not really. I haven’t heard voices or seen things like that. It’s more that I notice patterns in what people do or say, and I feel like there’s intent behind it.

Aside from this situation at work, would you say you've generally had a hard time trusting people—friends, family, even people you've just met—for most of your life, or is this suspicion pretty specific to your colleagues from this commission?

It’s pretty specific to the people from that commission, honestly. I don’t think I’ve always been someone who mistrusts everyone. This started after that project, when certain schedule changes, seating decisions, and comments in rehearsal started feeling like they were aimed at undermining me. Even when they show me emails or explanations, it still feels deliberate.

Over the past two years, have you also noticed distinct periods where your mood was unusually high, energetic, or irritable, or alternately periods of deep depression, that seemed to coincide with these suspicious feelings?

I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve been stressed and upset about it at times, definitely, but I haven’t noticed clear periods where I was unusually high-energy or really depressed that lined up with it. It’s more that the suspicion has just kind of stayed there.

Outside of this situation with your colleagues, how have things been going in other areas of your life—like taking care of yourself day-to-day, your other relationships, or your ability to keep up with responsibilities?

Outside of that, I think I’m functioning pretty normally. I’m still meeting deadlines, keeping up with composing, and I run most mornings. Things at home with my wife are basically steady too. It’s really this issue with the ensemble that’s been the problem.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports a fixed, encapsulated persecutory belief (colleagues undermining her) lasting nearly 2 years, with denial of hallucinations, disorganized speech, or negative symptoms. No manic/depressive episodes have coincided with the belief, ruling out a mood-related psychotic disorder. The suspicion is circumscribed to a specific group rather than a pervasive, lifelong pattern of distrust, arguing against paranoid personality disorder.
